title: Dummy renderer: shader and material RID owners are not thread-safe; materials made on a thread under `--headless` leak RIDs or crash at exit
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.7.2.stable (Arch Linux package, ed1daf0bf)

### System information

Linux (CachyOS, kernel 7.2), AMD Ryzen 5 7500F (6 cores / 12 threads), `--headless` (dummy rendering server)

### Issue description

The dummy renderer's material storage declares its RID owners without the thread-safe flag (`servers/rendering/dummy/storage/material_storage.h`):

```cpp
mutable RID_Owner<DummyShader> shader_owner;
...
mutable RID_Owner<DummyMaterial> material_owner;
```

The Forward+/Mobile and Compatibility storages declare theirs thread-safe (`RID_Owner<Shader, true> shader_owner;` in `renderer_rd/storage_rd/material_storage.h` and `drivers/gles3/storage/material_storage.h`). But RIDs are allocated on the calling thread (`RenderingServerDefault::shader_create_from_code()` calls `shader_allocate()` directly; `material_create` is `FUNCRIDSPLIT`), so under `--headless` a thread that creates materials races with the main thread doing the same. `BaseMaterial3D` makes this easy to hit: `get_rid()` runs `_update_shader()` on the calling thread, while the `BaseMaterial3D::flush_changes` idle callback creates and frees the generated shaders of dirty materials on the main thread.

The race corrupts the owner's `alloc_count` and free list. With the project below, every run prints errors like

```
ERROR: Attempting to initialize the wrong RID
ERROR: Parameter "mem" is null.
ERROR: Attempting to use an uninitialized RID
ERROR: Parameter "material" is null.
ERROR: Parameter "shader" is null.
```

and at exit

```
ERROR: 36 RID allocations of type 'N13RendererDummy15MaterialStorage13DummyMaterialE' were leaked at exit.
ERROR: 56 RID allocations of type 'N13RendererDummy15MaterialStorage11DummyShaderE' were leaked at exit.
```

In a real project, where only a few RIDs race, the count can also end up one too low; the last `shader_free()` at shutdown then decrements `alloc_count` below zero and writes out of bounds (`rid_owner.h:364`), which crashes. Symbolized stack of such a crash (SIGSEGV in `RID_Alloc::free`, then `abort()` from the crash handler), on quit after a headless run whose loader thread built materials:

```
#7  RID_Alloc<RendererDummy::MaterialStorage::DummyShader, false>::free (...) at ./core/templates/rid_owner.h:364
#8  RID_Owner<RendererDummy::MaterialStorage::DummyShader, false>::free (...) at ./core/templates/rid_owner.h:549
#9  RendererDummy::MaterialStorage::shader_free (...) at servers/rendering/dummy/storage/material_storage.cpp:158
#10 RendererDummy::Utilities::free (...) at servers/rendering/dummy/storage/utilities.cpp:66
#11 RenderingServerDefault::_free (...) at servers/rendering/rendering_server_default.cpp:56
#12 Shader::~Shader (...)
#17 ShaderMaterial::~ShaderMaterial (...) at scene/resources/material.cpp:550
#20 Ref<ShaderMaterial>::unref (this=... <TexturePreview::texture_material>)
#21 TexturePreview::finish_shaders () at editor/scene/texture/texture_editor_plugin.cpp:94
#22 unregister_editor_types () at editor/register_editor_types.cpp:339
#23 Main::cleanup (p_force=false) at main/main.cpp:5289
```

(`TexturePreview`'s shader is simply the last one freed; it is not involved in the race.)

This is probably the cause of #104118 (the same `DummyShader` leak on a headless export, which loads resources on worker threads). #124139 is the same problem for the dummy `texture_owner`; the dummy `mesh_owner` and `multimesh_owner` are declared the same way. Declaring these owners thread-safe, as the other renderers do, should fix it (not tested on a build here).

### Steps to reproduce

1. A project whose `project.godot` contains only `config_version=5`, and `repro.gd` below.
2. `godot --headless --path . --script repro.gd` (runs about 3 s of churn; the error output makes it take longer).
3. Errors as above in every run (6 of 6 here). With the worker thread left out (`_thread.start` removed, the main thread churning alone for the same time), 0 errors in 2 of 2 runs.

```gdscript
## A worker thread and the main thread both make StandardMaterial3Ds with changing settings, so both
## create and free the materials' generated shaders.
extends SceneTree

const SECONDS := 3.0

var _thread := Thread.new()
var _end := 0


func _initialize() -> void:
	_end = Time.get_ticks_msec() + int(SECONDS * 1000)
	_thread.start(_churn)


func _churn() -> void:
	while Time.get_ticks_msec() < _end:
		_material()


func _process(_delta: float) -> bool:
	for i in 50:
		_material()
	if _thread.is_alive():
		return false
	_thread.wait_to_finish()
	return true


## One material with a random key: a new key makes a shader, the last user of a key frees it.
func _material() -> void:
	var m := StandardMaterial3D.new()
	m.transparency = randi() % 4
	m.shading_mode = randi() % 3
	m.billboard_mode = randi() % 4
	m.cull_mode = randi() % 3
	m.vertex_color_use_as_albedo = randf() < 0.5
	m.get_rid()
```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

The two files above (`project.godot` with `config_version=5`, and `repro.gd`).
